detail.longDescription: I would like to add constraints to a generic type based on an associated type. I believe code speaks better than words, so here is an example: trait A { type Generic<T>; } trait B: A<Generic<T>=T> {} This is the simplemst version I could create that reproduces the error. The compiler tells me that T is not in scope, because it isn't... However, adding a type T into B so that it is B<T> would make B include something that it should not care about. I know a similar version of the problem but with lifetimes is easily solved by using for<'a> , but this doesn't work (as far as I know) for generic type instead of lifetime.
